ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, point $O$ is on the line $AC$, $OD$ bisects $\angle AOB$, $\angle BOE = \frac{1}{2}\angle EOC$, and $\angle DOE = 70^\circ$. Find the measure of $\angle EOC$.
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Let $\angle EOC = \alpha$ \\
Since $\angle BOE = \frac{1}{2} \angle EOC$ \\
Thus $\angle BOE = \frac{1}{2} \alpha$ \\
Since $\angle DOE = 70^\circ$ \\
Thus $\angle BOD = \angle DOE - \angle BOE = 70^\circ - \frac{1}{2} \alpha$ \\
Since $OD$ bisects $\angle AOB$ \\
Thus $\angle AOD = \angle BOD = 70^\circ - \frac{1}{2} \alpha$ \\
Since point O is on line AC, \\
Thus $\angle AOC = 180^\circ$ \\
Therefore $\angle EOC + \angle DOE + \angle AOD = 180^\circ$ \\
Therefore $\alpha + 70^\circ + 70^\circ - \frac{1}{2}\alpha = 180^\circ$ \\
Therefore $\alpha = 80^\circ$ \\
Therefore $\angle EOC = \boxed{80^\circ}$

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, C, O, and A are on the same horizontal straight line, O is in the middle, OC points to the left, and OA points to the right; from O upward, three more rays are drawn, which, in order from right to left, are OD, OB, and OE, respectively, so OB is located inside ∠DOE, and ∠AOD, ∠DOE, and ∠EOC together form the straight angle ∠AOC. Reasoning: Let x = ∠EOC. According to the problem, ∠BOE = x/2. Because in the figure OB is inside ∠DOE, ∠DOE = ∠DOB + ∠BOE, so ∠DOB = 70° - x/2. Also because OD bisects ∠AOB, ∠AOD = ∠DOB = 70° - x/2. Since A, O, and C are collinear, ∠AOC = 180°, and ∠AOD + ∠DOE + ∠EOC = 180°. Therefore (70° - x/2) + 70° + x = 180°, simplifying gives 140° + x/2 = 180°, hence x/2 = 40°, x = 80°. Therefore ∠EOC = 80°.
